```{r}
# Load these packages first
library(data.table)
library(rlang)
packageVersion("data.table")
packageVersion("rlang")

# Installing packages
package_install = function(package_list) {
  for (pkg in package_list) {
    if (!requireNamespace(pkg, quietly = TRUE)) {
      tryCatch({
        install.packages(pkg)
      }, error = function(e) {
        message(paste0("Could not install ", pkg, ": ", e))
      })
    }
    # Load the library
    library(pkg, character.only = TRUE)
  }
}
```

```{r}
# Removing certain columns (alternative outcomes) prior to imputation
cope_auo$gad_score_avg_may  = NULL
cope_auo$gad_score_may      = NULL  
cope_auo$gad_score_avg_june = NULL
cope_auo$gad_score_june     = NULL
cope_auo$'H1_Public information campaigns' = NULL
cope_auo$'C8EV_International travel controls' = NULL
cope_auo$'date_of_birth' = NULL
cope_auo$'zip_code' = NULL 
cope_auo$'date_of_birth' = NULL
cope_auo$sex_at_birth = NULL
cope_auo$age_bin = NULL

# Converting character columns to factor
cope_auo$gender = as.factor(cope_auo$gender)
cope_auo$race   = as.factor(cope_auo$race)
cope_auo$college_graduated  = as.factor(cope_auo$college_graduated)
cope_auo$married_or_with_sb = as.factor(cope_auo$married_or_with_sb)
cope_auo$home_ownership = as.factor(cope_auo$home_ownership)

# Checking column names and header
colnames(cope_auo)
head(cope_auo)
```


```{r}
set.seed(42)
data_split = initial_split(cope_auo, prop = 0.80, strata = "gad_score_avg_july")

# Extract training and testing sets
train_data = training(data_split)
test_data = testing(data_split)

# Print dimensions
print(paste0("Dimensions of train_data: ", dim(train_data)[1], " rows and ", dim(train_data)[2], " columns"))
print(paste0("Dimensions of test_data: ", dim(test_data)[1], " rows and ", dim(test_data)[2], " columns"))

# Convert to data.frames
train_data_df = as.data.frame(train_data)
test_data_df = as.data.frame(test_data)

# Impute missing values in training data
impute_train = missForest(train_data_df, maxiter = 200)
train_imputed = impute_train$ximp

# Impute missing values in test data using training data as reference
test_imputed = missForest(test_data_df, xtrue = train_imputed, maxiter = 200)$ximp
```


```{r}
# Check for any remaining missing values in training set
sum(is.na(train_imputed))

# Check for any remaining missing values in test set
sum(is.na(test_imputed))

# Comparing summary statistics before and after imputation for a few key variables
summary(train_data$gad_score_avg_july)
summary(train_data$college_graduated)
summary(train_data$married_or_with_sb)

summary(train_imputed$gad_score_avg_july)
summary(train_imputed$college_graduated)
summary(train_imputed$married_or_with_sb)

# Convert imputed data back to data.tables
train_imputed_dt = as.data.table(train_imputed)
test_imputed_dt = as.data.table(test_imputed)

# Add a column to identify the source of each row
train_imputed_dt[, source := "train"]
test_imputed_dt[, source := "test"]

# Combine the imputed training and testing sets
cope_auo_imputed = rbindlist(list(train_imputed_dt, test_imputed_dt), use.names = TRUE, fill = TRUE)

# Verify the dimensions of the rejoined dataset
print(paste0("Dimensions of cope_auo_imputed: ", dim(cope_auo_imputed)[1], " rows and ", dim(cope_auo_imputed)[2], " columns"))
```

```{r}

```


```{r}
# Subset the data
covid_subset = cope_raw_stringency %>%
  filter(Date >= "2020-03-11" & Date <= "2020-06-30")

# Select relevant columns
columns_of_interest = c("Date", "RegionName", "C1M_School_closing", "C2M_Workplace_closing", 
                         "C3M_Cancel_public_events", "C4M_Restrictions_on_gatherings", 
                         "C5M_Close_public_transport", "C6M_Stay_at_home_requirements", 
                         "C7M_Restrictions_on_internal_movement")

covid_subset = covid_subset %>%
  select(all_of(columns_of_interest))

head(covid_subset)
str(covid_subset)
```


```{r}
# Reshape the data
covid_long = covid_subset %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = -c(Date, RegionName), names_to = "Measure", values_to = "Value")

str(covid_long)
head(covid_long)
```


```{r}
# Calculate average stringency across states for each date and measure
covid_avg = covid_long %>%
  group_by(Date, Measure) %>%
  summarize(AvgValue = mean(Value, na.rm = TRUE),
            MinValue = min(Value, na.rm = TRUE),
            MaxValue = max(Value, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
  ungroup()
```

```{r}
# The solid line represents the average stringency across all states for each measure.
# The shaded area shows the range of stringency values across states, giving an idea of the variation between states.

ggplot(covid_avg, aes(x = Date, y = AvgValue)) +
  geom_line(aes(color = Measure), linewidth = 1) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = MinValue, ymax = MaxValue, fill = Measure), alpha = 0.3) +
  scale_x_date(date_labels = "%b", date_breaks = "1 month") +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 4, by = 1)) +
  labs(title = "COVID-19 Stringency Measures Over Time (State Averages)",
       x = "Month (2020)",
       y = "Average Stringency Level") +
  theme_classic() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom",
        legend.title = element_blank()) +
  facet_wrap(~ Measure, scales = "free_y", ncol = 2)
```



```{r}
# Function to analyze C4M and C5M measures
analyze_c4m_c5m = function(data) {
  results = data %>%
    filter(Measure %in% c("C4M_Restrictions_on_gatherings", "C5M_Close_public_transport")) %>%
    group_by(RegionName, Measure) %>%
    summarize(
      AvgStringency = mean(Value, na.rm = TRUE),
      ZeroStringency = all(Value == 0),
      .groups = "drop"
    ) %>%
    group_by(Measure) %>%
    summarize(
      TotalStates = n_distinct(RegionName),
      StatesWithZeroStringency = sum(ZeroStringency),
      AvgStringencyAcrossStates = mean(AvgStringency, na.rm = TRUE),
      StringencyDistribution = list(table(AvgStringency)),
      .groups = "drop"
    )
  
  return(results)
}

# Analyze C4M and C5M
c4m_c5m_analysis = analyze_c4m_c5m(covid_long)

# Print results
print(c4m_c5m_analysis)
```


```{r}
analyze_c4m_c5m = function(data) {
  start_date = as.Date("2020-03-15")
  end_date = as.Date("2020-06-30")
  
  results = data %>%
    filter(Measure %in% c("C4M_Restrictions_on_gatherings", "C5M_Close_public_transport"),
           Date >= start_date, Date <= end_date) %>%
    group_by(RegionName, Measure) %>%
    summarize(
      AlwaysZero = all(Value == 0),
      AlwaysOne = all(Value == 1),
      AlwaysTwo = all(Value == 2),
      AlwaysThree = all(Value == 3),
      AlwaysFour = all(Value == 4),
      .groups = "drop"
    ) %>%
    group_by(Measure) %>%
    summarize(
      TotalStates = n_distinct(RegionName),
      StatesAlwaysZero = sum(AlwaysZero),
      StatesAlwaysOne = sum(AlwaysOne),
      StatesAlwaysTwo = sum(AlwaysTwo),
      StatesAlwaysThree = sum(AlwaysThree),
      StatesAlwaysFour = sum(AlwaysFour),
      StatesAlwaysZeroList = list(RegionName[AlwaysZero]),
      StatesAlwaysOneList = list(RegionName[AlwaysOne]),
      StatesAlwaysTwoList = list(RegionName[AlwaysTwo]),
      StatesAlwaysThreeList = list(RegionName[AlwaysThree]),
      StatesAlwaysFourList = list(RegionName[AlwaysFour]),
      .groups = "drop"
    )
  
  return(results)
}

# Analyze C4M and C5M
c4m_c5m_analysis = analyze_c4m_c5m(covid_long)

# Print results
print(c4m_c5m_analysis)
print(c4m_c5m_analysis$StatesAlwaysThree)
print(c4m_c5m_analysis$StatesAlwaysFour)
```


```{r}
# Modified function to plot stringency distribution
plot_stringency_distribution = function(data, measure) {
  dist_data = data %>%
    filter(Measure == measure) %>%
    group_by(Value) %>%
    summarize(Count = n(), .groups = "drop")
  
  # Create stringency bins
  dist_data = dist_data %>%
    mutate(StringencyBin = cut(Value, 
                               breaks = c(-Inf, 0, 1, 2, 3, Inf),
                               labels = c("0", "0-1", "1-2", "2-3", "3-4"),
                               include.lowest = TRUE))
  
  # Summarize data by bins
  binned_data = dist_data %>%
    group_by(StringencyBin) %>%
    summarize(TotalCount = sum(Count), .groups = "drop")
  
  # Create the plot
  ggplot(binned_data, aes(x = StringencyBin, y = TotalCount)) +
    geom_bar(stat = "identity", fill = "steelblue") +
    geom_text(aes(label = TotalCount), vjust = -0.5) +  # Add count labels
    labs(title = paste("Distribution of Stringency -", measure),
         x = "Stringency Level",
         y = "Number of State-Days") +
    theme_classic() +
    theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 0, hjust = 0.5))  # Ensure x-axis labels are readable
}

# Create and save plots for C4M and C5M
c4m_plot = plot_stringency_distribution(covid_long, "C4M_Restrictions_on_gatherings")
c5m_plot = plot_stringency_distribution(covid_long, "C5M_Close_public_transport")

# Regenerating plots
c4m_plot
c5m_plot
```

```{r}
generate_exposure_windows = function(data, granularity, covid_start, outcome_start, 
                                    columns_of_interest, summary_function = "round_mean") {
  
  setDT(data)  # Convert to data.table if not already
  
  # Calculate the number of start date options
  exposure_start_range = as.numeric(outcome_start - covid_start)
  start_date_options = floor(exposure_start_range / granularity)
  
  # Create a list to store results
  results = list()
  
  # Counter for combinations
  combination_count = 0
  
  # Outer loop: start date
  for (i in 0:(start_date_options - 1)) {
    start_date_i = covid_start + days(i * granularity)
    
    # Calculate the number of duration options for this start date
    max_duration = as.numeric(outcome_start - start_date_i)
    duration_options = floor(max_duration / granularity)
    
    # Inner loop: duration
    for (j in 1:duration_options) {
      duration_j = j * granularity
      end_date_j = start_date_i + days(duration_j - 1)
      
      # Subset the data for the current window
      window_data = data[Date >= start_date_i & Date <= end_date_j, 
                        c("RegionName", "Date", ..columns_of_interest)]
      
      # Calculate summary statistics based on the selected function
      if (summary_function == "mode") {
        # Define a mode function
        get_mode = function(x) {
          ux = unique(x)
          ux[which.max(tabulate(match(x, ux)))]
        }
        window_stats = window_data[, lapply(.SD, get_mode), 
                                  by = RegionName, 
                                  .SDcols = columns_of_interest]
      } else if (summary_function == "round_mean") {
        # Round the mean to the nearest integer
        window_stats = window_data[, lapply(.SD, function(x) round(mean(x, na.rm = TRUE))), 
                                  by = RegionName, 
                                  .SDcols = columns_of_interest]
                                            
      } else if (summary_function == "average") {
        # Calculate mean without rounding (keeping decimal points)
        window_stats = window_data[, lapply(.SD, function(x) mean(x, na.rm = TRUE)),
                                        by = RegionName,
                                        .SDcols = columns_of_interest]                                  
                                            
      } else {
        # Default to round_mean if an invalid option is provided
        warning("Invalid summary_function provided. Using 'round_mean' as default.")
        window_stats = window_data[, lapply(.SD, function(x) round(mean(x, na.rm = TRUE))), 
                                  by = RegionName, 
                                  .SDcols = columns_of_interest]
      }      
     
      # Create the new key for this window
      window_key = sprintf("%s_%s_dur%d", 
                          format(start_date_i, "%Y%m%d"),
                          format(end_date_j, "%Y%m%d"),
                          duration_j)
      
      # Store the result with metadata
      results[[window_key]] = list(
        start_date = start_date_i,
        end_date = end_date_j,
        duration = duration_j,
        data = window_stats 
      )
      
      combination_count = combination_count + 1
    }
  }
  
  # Print the number of combinations
  print(sprintf("Generated %d combinations of start and end dates.", combination_count))
  
  return(results)
}
```

```{r}
combine_exposure_individual_data = function(exposure_windows, cope_auo) {
  # Create a lookup table from cope_auo with required columns
  lookup_table = cope_auo %>%
    select(person_id, RegionName, gad_score_avg_july, age_2020, 
           has_health_insurance, household_income_cat, have_job)

  # Initialize the result list
  combined_exposure_data = list()

  # Loop through each exposure window
  for (window_name in names(exposure_windows)) {
    # Get the current window data
    window_data = exposure_windows[[window_name]]$data

    # Perform a left join of lookup_table with window_data
    combined_data = lookup_table %>%
      left_join(window_data, by = "RegionName") %>%
      # Move RegionName to the beginning of the dataframe
      select(RegionName, everything())

    # Store the result in the new list
    combined_exposure_data[[window_name]] = list(
      start_date = exposure_windows[[window_name]]$start_date,
      end_date = exposure_windows[[window_name]]$end_date,
      duration = exposure_windows[[window_name]]$duration,
      data = combined_data
    )
  }

  return(combined_exposure_data)
}

combined_exposure_data = combine_exposure_individual_data(exposure_windows, cope_auo)
```

```{r}
# Function to check distributions for specified columns in a specific window
check_distributions = function(combined_data, window_name, columns_to_check) {
  # Get the data for the specified window
  window_data = combined_data[[window_name]]$data
  
  # Check each requested column
  for (col in columns_to_check) {
    if (col %in% names(window_data)) {
      cat("\n--------------------------------------------------")
      cat("\nDistribution for", col, "in window", window_name, ":\n")
      
      if (is.numeric(window_data[[col]])) {
        # For numeric columns, show summary first
        print(summary(window_data[[col]]))
        cat("\nAverage value of policy during exposure window:\n")
      }
      
      # Show actual distribution (not rounded) for any column type
      print(table(window_data[[col]], useNA = "ifany"))
    } else {
      cat("\nColumn", col, "not found in window", window_name, "\n")
    }
  }
}
```

```{r}
# Function to remove NA values in C1-C7 columns for all windows
remove_na_policy_rows = function(combined_data) {
  # Create new list to store cleaned data
  cleaned_data = list()
  
  # Policy columns to check for NAs
  policy_cols = c(
    "C1M_School_closing", "C2M_Workplace_closing", "C3M_Cancel_public_events", 
    "C4M_Restrictions_on_gatherings", "C5M_Close_public_transport", 
    "C6M_Stay_at_home_requirements", "C7M_Restrictions_on_internal_movement"
  )
  
  # Process each window
  for (window_name in names(combined_data)) {
    # Get window metadata
    window_info = combined_data[[window_name]]
    
    # Get data for this window
    window_data = window_info$data
    
    # Count rows before filtering
    rows_before = nrow(window_data)
    
    # Remove rows with NA in any of the policy columns
    window_data_clean = window_data %>%
      filter(if_all(all_of(policy_cols), ~!is.na(.)))
    
    # Count rows after filtering
    rows_after = nrow(window_data_clean)
    rows_removed = rows_before - rows_after
    
    # Print removal summary
    cat(sprintf("Window %s: Removed %d rows with NAs (%.2f%%)\n", 
                window_name, rows_removed, (rows_removed/rows_before)*100))
    
    # Store cleaned data with original metadata
    cleaned_data[[window_name]] = list(
      start_date = window_info$start_date,
      end_date = window_info$end_date,
      duration = window_info$duration,
      data = window_data_clean
    )
  }
  
  return(cleaned_data)
}

# Apply the function to clean all windows
combined_exposure_data_clean = remove_na_policy_rows(combined_exposure_data)

# Verify the cleaning for the first window
first_window = names(combined_exposure_data_clean)[1]
first_window_data_clean = combined_exposure_data_clean[[first_window]]$data

# Check the dimensions
cat("\nOriginal rows:", nrow(combined_exposure_data[[first_window]]$data), "\n")
cat("Cleaned rows:", nrow(first_window_data_clean), "\n")

# Check that there are no more NAs in the policy columns
policy_cols = c("C1M_School_closing", "C2M_Workplace_closing", "C3M_Cancel_public_events", 
                "C4M_Restrictions_on_gatherings", "C5M_Close_public_transport", 
                "C6M_Stay_at_home_requirements", "C7M_Restrictions_on_internal_movement",
               "RegionName")

cat("\nNA counts in cleaned data:\n")
sapply(policy_cols, function(col) sum(is.na(first_window_data_clean[[col]])))
```

```{r}
# First, verify the file is created locally
if (!file.exists(exposure_filename)) {
  stop("Local file not created successfully")
}

# Create a function to handle file copying and verification
verify_bucket_copy = function(filename, bucket_path) {
  # Define the full bucket path
  full_bucket_path = paste0(bucket_path, "/data/", filename)
  
  # Copy file to bucket
  copy_result = system(paste0("gsutil cp ./", filename, " ", bucket_path, "/data/"), intern=TRUE)
  
  # Verify copy was successful
  file_extension = tools::file_ext(filename)
  ls_result = system(paste0("gsutil ls ", bucket_path, "/data/*.", file_extension), intern=TRUE)
  
  # Check if file exists in bucket
  if (!any(grepl(filename, ls_result))) {
    warning(paste("File", filename, "not found in bucket"))
    return(list(success = FALSE, path = NULL))
  }
  return(list(success = TRUE, path = full_bucket_path))
}

# Execute the verification process
tryCatch({
  # Copy and verify exposure data
  verification_result = verify_bucket_copy(exposure_filename, my_bucket)
  
  # Print verification results
  if (verification_result$success) {
    message("File successfully copied and verified in bucket")
    message(paste("File location:", verification_result$path))
  } else {
    warning("File may not have been copied successfully")
  }
}, error = function(e) {
  stop(paste("Error in bucket operations:", e$message))
})
}
```
